title: Boundary formulas for every Z with ProdChar(X, Z), and finite boundary mass of [[0,1]]×X for normal X (supplied steps 9–10)
statement: (II) For all m, every X ∈ D_0(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, every Z ∈ D_{0+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), every ψ ∈ D^0(ℝ^{m+1}) and all ψ₀, ψ₁ ∈ D^0(ℝ^m) with ψ_i(x)(v) = ψ(cons(i,x))(fun l => ι(v l)) for all x, v (i = 0, 1): ∂Z(ψ) = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀). (III) For all m, j, every X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞, every Z ∈ D_{j+1+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z), every ψ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^{m+1}), all ψ₀, ψ₁ ∈ D^{j+1}(ℝ^m) with ψ_i(x)(v) = ψ(cons(i,x))(fun l => ι(v l)) for all x, v (i = 0, 1), and every φ : ℝ → D^j(ℝ^m) with φ(s)(x)(v) = ψ(cons(s,x))(Fin.cons e₀ (fun l => ι(v l))) for s ∈ [0,1] and all x, v: ∂Z(ψ) = X(ψ₁) − X(ψ₀) − ∫_0^1 ∂X(φ(s)) ds. (N) For all m, k, every X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ and every Z ∈ D_{k+1}(ℝ^{m+1}) with ProdChar(X, Z): if M(∂Y) < ∞ for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, then M(∂Z) < ∞. ProdChar(X, Z) is as in conjunct (a) of product_exists; D^q = TestFormOn univ q, D_q = GeometricCurrentOn univ q, M = mass, ∂ = boundary, cons, ι, e₀ as above.
